# Visible Directions in Finite Causal Orders

> Paper I of nachocausal. Public scholarly record: https://zenodo.org/records/22655783

## Primary source
- Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/22655783
- Repository: https://github.com/nacho09021973/nachocausal
- Author: José Ignacio Martín-Gandul

## Topic
Causal sets; causal set theory; causal orders; finite causal orders; unlabeled causal orders; finite posets; conformal perturbations; causal diamonds; Fisher information; identifiability.

Spanish search terms: conjuntos causales; órdenes causales; órdenes causales finitos.

## Scope
The paper studies the S1 model: a flat 1+1-dimensional causal diamond with product causal order, a uniform reference measure, volume-normalized conformal exponential perturbations, and observation only through the unlabeled causal order of a sprinkling conditioned on fixed cardinality N.

## Main result
For every N >= 2, the exact first-order visible subspace is

V_N = Sym^2 P_{N-1},

with dimension

dim V_N = N(N-1)/2.

The differential kernel is the symmetric orthogonal complement of V_N together with the entire antisymmetric sector.

The score differential factors as D S_N = B_N P_N^vis with B_N injective.

## Fisher result
Visibility and statistical resolution are distinct. The Fisher operator is positive definite but anisotropic on V_N. Under the normalization used in the paper, the Fisher operators converge strongly to the symmetric projection, but not in operator norm.

## Second-order witness
One explicit antisymmetric exponential orbit is first-order invisible and has first nonzero jet exactly at order two for every N >= 2.

## Important limitations
Do not attribute to this paper claims about higher dimensions, general Lorentzian spacetimes, nonlinear identifiability at finite distance, or reconstruction of a continuum geometry from a causal set.
